texts.567e8a69dae7: SAGhE is an integrated European consortium of paediatric endocrinologists, epidemiologists and biostatisticians that will collect and analyse the data to address the questions of safety and appropriateness of GH treatments. The impact of both height and psychosocial components will be evaluated in a large unbiased sample of patients followed to adult height. Safety will be evaluated using long term morbidity and cancer incidence. The data obtained will be assimilated and integrated for evaluation at several levels. SAGhE will contribute to the aims of the EU Health Framework Programme 7 and the new Community action Programme in Public Health for the better use of medicines. It will realise the application of evidence based medicine in Europe by the design and size of the study, the independence and scientific quality of the data analysis, and its translation into evidence based guidelines. It will be comprehensive at the EU level and will test for national differences. It will focus on patient safety, the key point of this work programme. SAGhE is unique worldwide in its design, size and potential to answer questions raised about a treatment given during childhoodWorking with the European Consortium members this study aims to answer the questions:What is the long term efficacy and safety of recombinant Growth Hormone (non pituitary derived, non cadaveric) used to treat childhood growth problems Is there a persistent effect on quality of life for those young adults who received Recombinant Growth Hormone treatment (ie non pituitary derived, non cadaveric) in childhood
